references.text: The original instruction regarding the Feast of Unleavened Bread given at the time of the Exodus from Egypt, where the Israelites were to eat unleavened bread for seven days.
Reiterates the command to eat unleavened bread for seven days and that no leaven shall be seen in the land.
The Feast of Unleavened Bread mentioned among the three major annual festivals in Israel.
The renewal of the covenant includes the command regarding the Feast of Unleavened Bread in the month of Abib.
Detailed instructions concerning the offerings during the Feast of Unleavened Bread, which lasts seven days from the fifteenth day of the first month.
The command to eat unleavened bread for seven days, called the bread of affliction, as a reminder of the Exodus from Egypt.
The conclusion of the festival with a holy assembly on the seventh day.
King Hezekiah's celebration of the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days with great joy in Jerusalem.
The Israelites celebrated the Feast of Unleavened Bread with joy for seven days after returning from exile.
Ezekiel's prophetic vision concerning the future celebration of Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days.
The disciples prepared the Passover meal for Jesus on the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread mentioned in connection with the planning of Jesus' arrest.
The first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread when the Passover lamb was slaughtered.
The Feast of Unleavened Bread, called Passover, was approaching when Jesus was to suffer.
Peter was arrested during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
Paul sailed from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread, showing that the early church still observed this feast.
Paul uses the Feast of Unleavened Bread as a spiritual metaphor, where Christ is our Passover lamb and we should celebrate with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
